questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

People used to preserve

A-companionship in absentia 

B- letters for years as these humble pieces 

C- of paper afforded
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **BCA**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph starts with ***'people used to preserve'****. *Hence the next sentence should say **what they used to preserve (noun)**
 
• **'A'**** **starts with the **noun** ***'******companionship'***, **'B' **starts with the **noun *'letters'***, and **'C' **starts with the **preposition *'of'***, it can be either **'A' **or **'B'**
 
• Among **'A' **and **'B'**, if we choose **'A'**, both the options **ACB **and **ABC **would render the paragraph grammatically absurd and structurally meaningless. This is because both **A-B **and **A-C **in this order** **are grammatically incompatible phrases 
 
• However, if we choose **'B'**, while the order **BAC** gives a grammatically erratic paragraph due to **B-A **in that order being grammatically incompatible phrases, the order **BCA **gives a grammatically and semantically coherent paragraph

**Thus the correct answer is: ***People used to preserve letters for years as these humble pieces of paper afforded companionship in absentia*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word. **

Objective
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Prejudiced**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The word that is opposite in meaning to "Objective" is: Prejudiced
 
• "Objective" refers to being unbiased, impartial, or based on facts and evidence rather than personal opinions or prejudices. It indicates a neutral and fair approach to evaluating or assessing something.
 
• On the other hand, "Prejudiced" means having preconceived opinions or biases that may influence one's judgment or decision-making process. It signifies a lack of objectivity and fairness, as personal biases can cloud one's judgment.
 
• **Therefore, option 4) Prejudiced is the correct choice as it is opposite in meaning to "Objective."**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 

 
• **Fair**

 
 
• This option is not the opposite of "Objective." While fairness can be a desirable quality associated with objectivity, it does not inherently mean the opposite. One can be fair and objective at the same time.
 
 
 
• **Detached**
 
 
• This option is not the opposite of "Objective." "Detached" refers to being impartial or not emotionally involved, which can align with objectivity. Both detached and objective suggest a lack of personal bias or attachment to a particular outcome.
 
 
 
• **Straight**
 
 
• This option is not the opposite of "Objective." "Straight" typically refers to something that is direct, honest, or without deviation. It does not inherently represent the opposite of being objective.

questions.question: Which organ of the government consists of elected representatives of People?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Legislature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Legislature:

 
 
• The legislature is the organ of the government which formulates laws.
 
• Legislature enjoys a very special and important in every democratic state.
 
• It is the assembly of the elected representatives of the people and represents the national public opinion and the power of the people.
 
• In most states, the Legislature consists of the Governor and the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha). This means that these states have a unicameral Legislature.
 
• In a few states, there are two houses of the Legislature namely, the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) and Legislative council (Vidhan Parishad) besides the Governor. Where there are two Houses, the Legislature, is known as bicameral. 
 
 
 
• *Legislative Assembly:*
 
 
• There is a Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) in every State.
 
• It represents the people of the State.
 
• The members of Vidhan Sabha are directly elected by people on the basis of a universal adult franchise.
 
• They are directly elected by all adult citizens registered as voters in the State.
 
 

*From the above, it is clear that the ‘Legislature’ organ of the state refers to the elected representatives of the **People****.*

questions.question: Who gave the concept of ‘Separation of Powers’ related to different forms of governments?

__
 
• The concept of separation of powers was given by Montesquieu.
 
• Montesquieu described the separation of political power among a legislature, an executive, and a judiciary.
 
• He wrote that the government is morally obligated to serve people, namely by protecting their natural rights of life, liberty, and property

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** ** **__**Aristotle**__

__
 
• Aristotle was a philosopher as well as the pioneer of human knowledge.
 
• He was famous for his statement that "man is by nature a political animal."
 
• Aristotle conceived of politics as being like an organism rather than like a machine, and as a collection of parts none of which can exist without the others.
 
• He was also the propounder of Realism and was entirely opposed to the world of ideas.
 
• He believed in inculcating the habit of reasoning and critical thinking in students rather than just cramming bookish knowledge.

Plato__ (429–347 BCE)

__
 
• He is one of the most dazzling thinkers in the Western philosophical tradition and one of the most penetrating, wide-ranging, and influential authors in the history of philosophy.
 
• After the death of Socrates, Plato, the most famous of his pupils, carried on much of his former teacher's work and eventually founded his own school, the Academy, in 385 BCE.
 
• He wrote dialogues between Socrates and others that would explore philosophical issues. These dialogues would be used in his school as starting points for discussion.
 
• The Platonic dialogues consist of Socrates asking questions of another and proving, through these questions, that the other person has the wrong idea on the subject.

**Hobbes**__

 
• Thomas Hobbes was an English philosopher, considered to be one of the founders of modern political philosophy.
 
• He is best known for his 1651 book Leviathan, in which he expounds on an influential formulation of social contract theory.
